mainTopic: The scope of the סוטה's oath (which marriages and time periods it covers, and רבי מאיר's future oath), and whether a woman can drink the סוטה water twice.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about the oath the סוטה answers with "אמן אמן." Her oath covers every stage when she was bound to this man, including while waiting for a יבם and after ייבום. רבי מאיר adds that the oath also covers the future. Everyone agrees the oath cannot include the time before אירוסין or after a divorce. The rule is that the husband may include only a time when sinning would forbid her to him. In the גמרא, רב המנונא uses this to prove that a שומרת יבם who sinned is forbidden to her יבם, but the scholars of ארץ ישראל reject this and explain that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. Next, the גמרא rules that the oath may cover an earlier marriage (רבי ירמיה) and even a future remarriage (רב אשי). A ברייתא explains that for רבי מאיר, the water acts against her only if she later sins. Finally, a ברייתא brings three views on whether a woman can drink the water twice, and רבא begins to reconcile them with the פסוק. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The oath also covers her time as a שומרת יבם and after ייבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of the stages the oath covers, adding שומרת יבם and a woman married through ייבום. It closes with the core oath: she did not become defiled, and if she did, the curses should come upon her.
steps.simpleTranslation: [I did not stray as an engaged woman or a married woman,] nor while waiting for my יבם, nor once married to him. Amen that I did not become defiled, and if I did, may [the curses] come upon me.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing the list of life stages the סוטה swears about. Then it states the main line of her oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath covers every stage when she was forbidden to other men because of this husband or this marriage bond: ארוסה, נשואה, שומרת יבם, and כנוסה. This is the first meaning of the double אמן: it covers all these stages. The closing words "יבואו בי" show she accepts the curses if she is lying.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do ייבום
Brought in, meaning married to the יבם through ייבום
I became defiled, meaning I was with another man
May they come upon me (the curses)

phrases.english: nor as a woman waiting for the yavam, nor when married to him.
Amen that I did not become defiled,
and if I did become defiled, may they come upon me.
phrases.notes: "They" means the curses of the oath that the כהן just read to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The סוטה's oath covers her time as ארוסה, נשואה, שומרת יבם, and כנוסה, and she accepts the curses if she was defiled.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the second אמן covers the future
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר explains the double אמן differently: one אמן is for the past (I did not become defiled) and one is for the future (I will not become defiled).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Amen that I did not become defiled, amen that I will not become defiled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives his own explanation of why she says אמן twice. He says the oath also covers the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion uses the two אמן's to cover different stages and cases from the past. רבי מאיר adds a new idea: the oath reaches forward in time. So if she becomes defiled later, the oath and its curses can still take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: I will become defiled (future tense)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that a husband can make conditions about future behavior, which the next line limits.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Amen that I did not become defiled,
phrases.notes: The two "amens" come from the פסוק in במדבר 5:22.

phrases.english: amen that I will not become defiled.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אָמֵן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְמֵאתִי, אָמֵן שֶׁלֹּא אֶטָּמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the double אמן than the first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double אמן covers both the past and the future.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: no conditions about before אירוסין or after divorce
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions agree the husband cannot include in the oath what she did before she was engaged to him or what she will do after she is divorced from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: All agree that he cannot make her swear about the time before she became engaged, or about the time after she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets the outer limits of the oath. Everyone agrees on this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath only covers the time when she was bound to this husband. Before אירוסין and after a divorce she is not his wife, so being with another man then does not make her forbidden to him. Even רבי מאיר, who includes the future, agrees the future stops at a divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
Makes a condition with her, adding something to the oath
That she becomes engaged (אירוסין)
That she becomes divorced

steps.confusionAlert: "מתנה" here is not "a gift" (מַתָּנָה). It is the verb "makes a condition."

phrases.english: All agree that he does not make a condition with her,
phrases.notes: "All" means both the first opinion and רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: not about before she becomes engaged
and not about after she becomes divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets limits that apply to both opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oath cannot include the time before אירוסין or the time after divorce.

steps.title: Defiled while divorced and later remarried: not included
steps.stepSummary: If she was secluded and defiled with another man while divorced, and her husband later remarried her, he cannot include that period in the oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she secluded herself with a man and became defiled, and afterward her husband took her back, he could not make her swear about that.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a practical example of the rule just stated. The time she was divorced stays outside the oath, even after he remarries her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that once he remarries her, he could ask about everything since their first marriage. But while divorced she was not his wife. Being with another man without marrying him does not forbid her to return to her first husband, so that time has nothing to do with the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: She secluded herself (with a man)
He took her back (remarried her)

steps.whatToRemember: The oath of the סוטה only covers the time she was bound to this husband: as ארוסה, נשואה, שומרת יבם, or כנוסה. רבי מאיר adds the future. No one includes the time before אירוסין or after divorce, even if he later remarries her.

phrases.english: If she secluded herself with someone and became defiled,
phrases.notes: This is talking about the time when she was divorced from her husband.

phrases.english: and afterward he took her back,
he could not make a condition with her about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִסְתְּרָה לְאֶחָד וְנִטְמֵאת, וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶחְזִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the "after divorce" limit to a case where the husband remarries her.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who remarries his divorced wife cannot include in the oath what she did while divorced.

steps.title: The general rule for what the oath can cover
steps.stepSummary: The משנה closes with a rule: the husband may only include in the oath a time when sinning would have made her forbidden to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: any situation where, if she had relations with another man, she would not become forbidden to her husband, he cannot include it in the oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up all the earlier cases (before engagement, after divorce, and so on) with one general rule. This rule becomes the key to the גמרא's discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oath only covers sins that would actually matter for this marriage. If an act would not forbid her to her husband, it has nothing to do with him, so he cannot make her swear about it. This explains why the earlier steps excluded the time before engagement and after divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the general rule
She has relations (with another man)
Includes it as a condition in her oath

steps.whatToRemember: The husband can only make her swear about a time when sinning would have forbidden her to him.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
Any case where she would have relations with another man
and she would not become forbidden to him (her husband)
he may not stipulate it with her (in the oath).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the cases in Steps 3 and 4 with one general principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband may only include in the oath periods when adultery would forbid her to him.

steps.title: רב המנונא: a שומרת יבם who sinned is forbidden to her יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with רב המנונא's ruling that a widow waiting for ייבום who committed adultery becomes forbidden to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא says: a widow waiting for her יבם who committed adultery becomes forbidden to her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a new ruling from רב המנונא about a שומרת יבם who sinned. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יבם is not yet fully married to the יבם. She is only tied to him. רב המנונא says that even this weaker tie is strong enough that adultery forbids her to him, just like a married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do ייבום
She committed adultery
Her יבם, the brother-in-law

steps.confusionAlert: She is not yet married to the יבם. The whole question is whether adultery forbids her even though the marriage has not happened yet.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Hamnuna says:
A widow awaiting her yavam who committed adultery
is forbidden to her yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a ruling built on the שומרת יבם case from Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומרת יבם who committed adultery becomes forbidden to her יבם.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא proves his ruling: the משנה lets the husband include the שומרת יבם period in the oath, and its own rule allows that only if sinning then would forbid her.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know? Because the משנה lists 'a שומרת יבם' and 'married through ייבום.' If she becomes forbidden, it makes sense that he can include it in the oath. But if she does not become forbidden, how could he include it? We learned that this is the rule: any case where sinning would not forbid her, he cannot include it in the oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רב המנונא's ruling and answers by putting two parts of the משנה together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Part one: the משנה says the husband can make her swear about the time she was a שומרת יבם. Part two: the משנה's rule says he can only do that for a time when sinning would forbid her. Put them together, and sinning as a שומרת יבם must forbid her to the יבם.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
From the fact that it teaches
It makes sense if you say

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
From the fact that it teaches: a widow awaiting her yavam, and one married through levirate marriage.
Granted, if you say she is forbidden,
that is why he may stipulate it with her,
but if you say she is not forbidden,
how can he stipulate it with her?
But didn't we learn: This is the principle:
Any case where, if she would have relations with another man,
she would not become forbidden to him,
he may not stipulate it with her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב המנונא's ruling in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's ruling that a שומרת יבם who sinned is forbidden to the יבם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's inclusion of שומרת יבם in the oath (Step 1), combined with its rule in Step 5.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל: the הלכה does not follow רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל rule that the הלכה is not like רב המנונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the West (ארץ ישראל): the הלכה is not like רב המנונא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that the scholars in ארץ ישראל reject רב המנונא's ruling for practical הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with רב המנונא's proof from the משנה, the practical ruling is that a שומרת יבם who sinned does not become forbidden to her יבם. The next two steps explain how this ruling deals with his proof from the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
The הלכה is not

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא proved from the משנה that a שומרת יבם who sinned is forbidden to her יבם, but in ארץ ישראל they ruled that the הלכה does not follow him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical outcome: adultery by a שומרת יבם does not forbid her to the יבם. Steps 9 and 10 then explain how the משנה's wording fits this ruling.

phrases.english: They say in the West:
The halakha is not in accordance with Rav Hamnuna.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the practical outcome of רב המנונא's ruling from Steps 6 and 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is not like רב המנונא. A שומרת יבם who committed adultery does not become forbidden to her יבם.

steps.title: Whose view is the משנה's mention of a שומרת יבם?
steps.stepSummary: Since the הלכה is not like רב המנונא, the גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows when it lets the husband include the שומרת יבם period in the oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says the oath can include the time she was a widow waiting for the יבם and the time she was married to him. Whose opinion is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars of ארץ ישראל just ruled against רב המנונא, so the גמרא pushes back: what about the משנה he used as proof? It asks whose view that line of the משנה follows, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא proved his rule from the משנה. If the הלכה is not like him, the משנה cannot speak for everyone. So the גמרא looks for a specific תנא whose view the משנה reflects.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow waiting for her late husband's brother (the יבם) to do ייבום or חליצה
Married, here meaning already taken in marriage by the יבם
Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: But that which is taught
"a widow waiting for the יבם, and one married to him"
whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the ruling against רב המנונא and asks how the משנה he relied on should be understood.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא the משנה follows when it includes the שומרת יבם period in the oath.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of the scholars of ארץ ישראל (step 8) that the הלכה is not like רב המנונא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets the husband include the שומרת יבם period in the oath. Its own rule (step 5) allows that only if sinning then would forbid her. So the משנה seems to support רב המנונא against the ruling of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who treats a woman forbidden by an ordinary לאו like an ערוה. So a שומרת יבם who sins becomes forbidden to the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רבי עקיבא. He holds that קידושין do not take effect even with women forbidden by an ordinary negative commandment, so he treats her like an ערוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא's view, and not everyone's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומרת יבם who is with another man breaks only a regular לאו. Most hold that this does not forbid her to the יבם. רבי עקיבא treats a לאו like an ערוה, so for him she becomes forbidden, just as a married woman who sins becomes forbidden to her husband. The הלכה does not follow him, which is why it does not follow רב המנונא either.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal does not take effect
Relationships forbidden by an ordinary negative commandment, not punished by כרת
A severely forbidden relationship, like a married woman or a close relative
He treats her as

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's mention of a שומרת יבם reflects רבי עקיבא alone, so it is not a proof for the הלכה.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Akiva
who says: betrothal does not take effect
with those forbidden by negative commandments
and he treats her like a forbidden relation
phrases.notes: "Her" is the waiting widow who sinned. For רבי עקיבא, her sin makes her forbidden to the יבם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 9 by attributing the משנה to רבי עקיבא alone.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who treats a woman forbidden by a לאו like an ערוה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a single תנא (רבי עקיבא), so it does not reflect the accepted הלכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's inclusion of a שומרת יבם follows רבי עקיבא, who treats a woman forbidden by a לאו like an ערוה. So it does not disprove the ruling of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Can the oath cover an earlier marriage?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks two questions. Can a husband who remarried his divorced wife make the oath cover their first marriage? Can a יבם make it cover her marriage to his late brother?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: may a man make the oath cover the first marriage? May he make it cover his brother's marriage? What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבי ירמיה asks whether the husband may stretch the oath back to a marriage that came before the current one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the man divorced his wife and later remarried her. In the second, a יבם married his brother's widow. In both, the earlier period was a real marriage, but not the current marriage. The question is whether he can make her swear she was faithful back then too.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question in search of an answer)
Make a condition, here meaning to add to the oath
The first marriage, before a divorce

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
May a man make a condition
phrases.notes: "Make a condition" here means requiring her oath to cover that time too.

phrases.english: about the first marriage?
About his brother's marriage, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about how far back the oath may reach.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the oath may include an earlier marriage, either his own before a divorce or his brother's.

steps.title: The משנה's rule answers: yes, he may
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's rule says he may include any time when sinning would have forbidden her. Sinning in either earlier marriage would have done so, so he may include both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: the rule is that whenever her sin would not forbid her to him, he could not include it. That implies that when it would forbid her, he can include it. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי ירמיה from the closing rule of the משנה (see step 5) and concludes that he may include these periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states its rule in the negative: if sinning would not forbid her, the time cannot be included. The גמרא reads the opposite side: if sinning would forbid her, it can be included. Adultery during the first marriage would have forbidden her to him forever. Adultery during the brother's marriage would have forbidden her to the brother and also to the יבם. So both periods may be included.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the rule
This implies (reading the opposite side of a statement)
Learn from this (the proof stands)

steps.whatToRemember: The test is whether a sin back then would have made her forbidden. If yes, the husband may include that time in the oath, even from an earlier marriage.

phrases.english: Come and hear: this is the rule:
In any case where, if she had relations with another man,
she would not become forbidden to him,
he could not include it with her.
This implies that if she would be forbidden,
then indeed he may include it.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from the משנה's closing rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Since sinning in either earlier marriage would have forbidden her, he may include those periods in the oath.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband may include an earlier marriage in the oath, his own or his brother's.

steps.title: How רבי מאיר's oath about the future works
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains רבי מאיר's "amen that I will not become defiled." The water does not judge her now for a future sin. It acts later, if and when she sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says רבי מאיר holds the second אמן means "I will not become defiled." A ברייתא teaches: he did not mean that if she will sin, the water checks her right now. He meant that when she does sin, the water she already drank will shake her and check her then.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, רבי מאיר's reading of the double "amen," and brings a ברייתא explaining how an oath about the future works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the water could punish her today for a sin she will commit later. The ברייתא rejects that idea. The water stays "waiting" inside her, and only if she sins later does it act against her and test her.

keyTerms.meaning: Amen: her acceptance of the oath
I became defiled (I was unfaithful)
Shake up or destabilize
Test or check

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רבי מאיר as saying the water punishes her now for a future sin. It acts only later, if she actually sins.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Amen that I did not become defiled, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." points to the rest of the משנה line: the second amen means "I will not become defiled."

phrases.english: It was taught: It is not that, when Rabbi Meir said
"amen that I will not become defiled," he meant
that if she will become defiled,
the water tests her from now.
Rather: when she becomes defiled,
the water shakes her and tests her.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אָמֵן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְמֵאתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה, רבי מאיר's reading of the double amen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An oath about the future does not trigger the water now. The water acts against her only if and when she later sins.

steps.title: Can the oath cover a future remarriage?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the husband may include in the oath a later marriage, in case he divorces her and remarries her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: May a man make the oath cover a later marriage? Do we say that right now, at least, she is not forbidden to him? Or maybe we look ahead, because sometimes a man divorces his wife and then takes her back?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new question that goes one step past רבי ירמיה's questions. Those were about earlier marriages. This one is about a marriage that has not happened yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule so far is that the husband may include any time when sinning would have made her forbidden to him. One side of the question says only the present marriage counts, since nothing forbids her now. The other side says a remarriage can really happen, and sinning during it would forbid her too.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question that had no ready answer
A later marriage, after a divorce and remarriage
Makes the oath cover something; includes it in the terms of the oath
Takes back; remarries his divorced wife

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
What is the law, may a man make his oath cover
a later marriage?
phrases.notes: He means a marriage that might come later, if he divorces her and then marries her again.

phrases.english: Do we say that now, at least, she is not forbidden to him,
or perhaps, since sometimes he divorces her
and then takes her back?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: מַהוּ שֶׁיַּתְנֶה אָדָם עַל נִישּׂוּאִין הָאַחֲרוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי ירמיה's questions about past marriages to a possible future marriage
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the oath can include a future remarriage that does not yet exist

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the oath's limits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the oath cannot cover the time before betrothal or the time after divorce. If she sinned while divorced and he took her back, he cannot include that time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Everyone agrees that he cannot make the oath cover the time before she was betrothed, or the time after she is divorced. If she secluded herself with a man and became defiled, and afterward he took her back, he cannot include that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה to answer רב אשי. This step only quotes the source. The inference that answers the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules out the divorce period because a sin during that time does not forbid her to him. The order of events in the משנה is the key: first she sins, then he takes her back. The גמרא will build its inference on that order.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
She becomes betrothed
He takes her back, remarrying her

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: הַכֹּל שָׁוִין שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מַתְנֶה עִמָּהּ
phrases.english: Everyone agrees that he cannot make the oath cover
neither the time before she was betrothed,
nor the time after she is divorced.
If she secluded herself with someone and became defiled,
and afterward he takes her back,
he cannot include that time.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַכֹּל שָׁוִין שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מַתְנֶה עִמָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the משנה as evidence to answer רב אשי
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's question about a future remarriage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of a woman who sinned while divorced and was then taken back

steps.title: Yes, the oath can cover a future remarriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the משנה that if he takes her back first and she sins afterward, he may include that in the oath. The question is resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if he takes her back and then she becomes defiled, he can indeed include that in the oath. Conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely and draws out the answer to רב אשי's question. Then it closes the question with "שמע מינה."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled out only a sin that came before the remarriage. The flip side is a sin that comes after the remarriage. Such a sin would forbid her, so the husband may include that future marriage in the oath now.

keyTerms.meaning: But this implies; introduces the opposite case that follows from the text
So too; indeed it is so
Conclude from it; the question is settled

steps.whatToRemember: The husband's oath can cover any marriage in which her sin would forbid her to him: past marriages, the present one, and even a future remarriage.

phrases.english: But if he takes her back and then she becomes defiled,
then indeed he can include it in the oath.
Conclude from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא יַחְזִירֶנָּה וְתִיטָּמֵא, הָכִי נָמֵי דְּמַתְנֵי. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the quoted משנה and resolves the question
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband may make the oath cover a future remarriage to the same wife

steps.title: A woman can drink the water more than once
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "זאת תורת הקנאות" that a woman may drink the סוטה water and drink it again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "This is the law of jealousy" teaches that a woman drinks and then drinks again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. Can a woman who already drank the water have to drink again if she becomes a סוטה again?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls it "the law" of jealousy. The ברייתא reads this as one law that applies every time there is a קינוי. So a second suspicion means a second drinking.

keyTerms.meaning: The law of jealousy, meaning the סוטה process
Drinks and drinks again

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"This is the law of jealousy"
teaches that the woman drinks and drinks again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the oath discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may be made to drink the סוטה water more than once

steps.title: רבי יהודה: she does not drink twice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads the word "זאת" as limiting: the woman does not drink a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: "This" teaches that the woman does not drink again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא. He reads the same פסוק the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion focused on "the law," one law for every case. רבי יהודה focuses on the word "זאת," which narrows things down. For him, it means the process happens only once.

keyTerms.meaning: "This"; here read as a limiting word

steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions use the very same פסוק. The disagreement is about which word in it to stress.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"This" teaches that the woman does not drink again.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: זֹאת, שֶׁאֵין הָאִשָּׁה שׁוֹתָה וְשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman does not drink the סוטה water a second time

steps.title: נחוניא's testimony: twice only with two husbands
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that נחוניא the ditch digger testified that she drinks again. They accepted this for two different husbands, but not for one husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a case in which נחוניא the ditch digger testified before us that the woman drinks and drinks again. We accepted his testimony for two men, but not for one man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a report of testimony that limits his own rule. A woman can drink again, but only when a different husband brings her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחוניא testified that a woman drinks a second time. רבי יהודה's court accepted this only when there are two husbands. If she drank in her first marriage, a second husband can make her drink again. The same husband cannot make her drink twice.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual case or incident
נחוניא the digger of ditches (water pits), the name of a sage
Testimony, here a report of a received teaching
With two men, meaning two different husbands

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, a woman can drink the סוטה water a second time only for a different husband, never twice for the same husband.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: There was an incident
and Nechunya the ditch digger testified before us
that the woman drinks and drinks again,
and we accepted his testimony for two men,
phrases.notes: "Two men" means two husbands: she drank for the first husband and must drink again for the second.

phrases.english: but not for one man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה וְהֵעִיד לְפָנֵינוּ נְחוּנְיָא חוֹפֵר שִׁיחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי יהודה's rule by allowing a second drinking with a different husband
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman drinks again for a second husband, but not twice for the same husband

steps.title: The חכמים: she never drinks twice
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the חכמים, who say a woman never drinks the סוטה water twice, with one husband or with two.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: A woman does not drink and drink again, whether it is the same husband or two different husbands.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its last opinion. The חכמים say a woman never drinks the water a second time, in any case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we had three views. The first תנא says she drinks again. רבי יהודה reports that נחוניא's teaching was accepted only for two husbands. The חכמים now take the strictest limiting position: even with two different husbands, she does not drink again.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages. Here this is the final, anonymous group of opinion in the ברייתא.
Drinks and repeats. She drinks the סוטה water a second time.
One man. Here this means the same husband.
Two men. Here this means two different husbands.

steps.whatToRemember: There are three positions in the ברייתא. The first תנא says she drinks again. רבי יהודה (through נחוניא) says only with two husbands. The חכמים say never.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
The woman does not drink and drink again,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּאִישׁ אֶחָד בֵּין בִּשְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים.
phrases.english: whether with one man or with two men.
phrases.notes: "Men" here means husbands. Even if she married someone else, who also warned her, she still doesn't drink again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that began in step 17, adding the third and strictest view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a סוטה never drinks a second time, with the same husband or a different one.

steps.title: How does each side handle the word that goes against it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both ends of the ברייתא. The first תנא ignores the limiting word "זאת", and the חכמים ignore the expanding word "תורת".
steps.simpleTranslation: But for the first תנא, isn't it written "זאת" ("this"), which limits? And for the later חכמים, isn't it written "תורת" ("the law of"), which includes more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a two-sided question. Each opinion seems to be ignoring a word in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "זאת תורת הקנאות". "תורת" was used to include drinking again, and "זאת" was used to limit it. The first תנא says she always drinks again, so what does he do with "זאת"? The חכמים say she never drinks again, so what do they do with "תורת"?

keyTerms.meaning: The first תנא. The opening, anonymous opinion in a ברייתא or משנה.
The later Rabbis. Here this means the חכמים mentioned at the end of the ברייתא.
But isn't it written? A formula for challenging someone from a פסוק.
"This." A word read as limiting.
"The law of." A word read as including more cases.

steps.confusionAlert: This one question attacks two different opinions. "זאת" is the problem for the first תנא, and "תורת" is the problem for the חכמים. Don't mix up which word challenges which side.

phrases.english: And according to the first תנא too,
isn't it written "this"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:29. He says she drinks again, so what does he do with the limiting word?

phrases.english: And according to the later Rabbis too,
isn't it written "the law of"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinions just laid out, using the words of the פסוק they were derived from.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first תנא (who ignores "זאת") and the חכמים (who ignore "תורת").
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each word in the פסוק must teach something. An opinion that leaves one of them unexplained looks like it goes against the פסוק.

steps.title: רבא begins: one husband, one suspected man
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts to answer by splitting the cases. With the same husband and the same suspected man, everyone agrees she does not drink again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When it is one husband and one suspected man, everyone agrees that the woman does not drink a second time,
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer to the double question. This is only the first part of his answer, and it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's approach is that the opinions don't clash on every case. In the simplest case, the same husband warns her again about the same man after she was already found innocent. Here "זאת" applies according to everyone, so she does not drink again. The disagreement must be about other cases, which רבא will go on to list.

keyTerms.meaning: The man she is suspected of being with.
Everyone agrees. Literally, the whole world does not argue.

phrases.english: Rava said:
With one husband and one suspected man,
everyone agrees
that the woman does not drink and drink again,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וּבוֹעֵל אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the double challenge of step 21 by dividing the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the opinions apply to different situations, so the פסוק's words are not ignored.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the first תנא and the חכמים each completely ignore one word of the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the case of one husband and one suspected man, all agree she does not drink again. The disagreement is limited to other cases (continued next).
